newsitem.title: USA: VimpelCom registers for secondary offering.
newsitem.headline: VimpelCom registers for secondary offering.

text.p: Vimpel-Communications said it filed a registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with a previously announced proposed secondary offering by FGI Wireless Ltd.

The company has proposed on April 21, 1997 to offer 3,458,000 American Depository Shares (ADS) representing 2,593,500 shares of VimpelCom common shares in the U.S. and Canada and FGI Wireless Ltd outside of the U.S. and Canada.
VimpelCom said it will not be issuing or selling shares in the offering.

FGI Wireless is a private U.S. company founded as an investment vehicle for non-Russian venture capitalists and institutions to invest in VimpelCom. FGI's sole material asset is 3,305,622 shares of VimpelCom common stock.

Since VimpleCom's initial public offering in November 1996, its common stock has increased in value and hence, so did the value of FGI's assets. VimpelCom's ADSs were trading at $30.88 on Wednesday, up from its initial public offering price of $20.50.
The investors in FGI have decided to liquidate and distribute FGI's assets to reduce the corporate-level taxes that would be payable with the sale or distribution of the VimpelCom stock.

The purpose of the proposed secondary sale is to obtain the cash necessary to pay the U.S. corporate-level taxes that will be incurred with the liquidation of FGI and the sale of the VimpelCom ADSs and to enable FGI to distribute either cash or ADSs to its investors at their election.
VimpelCom provides cellular telecommunications in Russia under the brand name "Bee Line."
